comment: Exercise 17.1: STRIDE analysis of the proposed read-only status page (tests/dashboard.dot).

threats.threat: Any device on the network reads the status as if it were the room display.
A web page that the operator opens in the same browser sends requests to the status page with the operator's stored token (cross-site request).
threats.note: The token travels in the Authorization header, never in a cookie, so the browser does not add it on its own; a cross-site script may set that header only after a CORS preflight (OPTIONS), which DASH-002 answers with 405. The page also has no state-changing request to forge.

threats.threat: Nobody can tell who tried to read the status with a wrong token.
A program on the PC answers on the status port before minidaq_server does and shows a false 'running, complete' status.
threats.note: The display verifies the server certificate; a false page without the key fails the handshake.

threats.threat: A crafted request changes the acquisition's state, for example a POST or a GET with a query string that reaches the control protocol.
The adapter's refusals leave no record, so a scan of the port goes unnoticed.
The page shows a token, a file path, or an exception's text to whoever can read it.
Slow clients that open connections and send nothing hold the adapter's connections, or a huge request exhausts memory, during a scan.
threats.note: The adapter runs in the control thread; the acquisition threads do not wait for it.

threats.threat: An observer token, or a defect in the adapter, is used to stop the scan through the status page.
threats.note: The adapter calls only status(); it has no path to the commands.

threats.threat: A machine between the display and the PC changes the page to show a healthy run that is in fact incomplete.
An eavesdropper reads the observer token from the Authorization header and the status from the response.
A flood of connections from the network keeps the room display from updating.
threats.assumption: The status page is reachable only on the scanner's own network, behind the site's firewall (threat-model.md, section 6, item 4).

threats.threat: The page is embedded in a frame of another site, which then reads or overlays it.
The room display denies having shown a status at a given time.
threats.note: The display shows; it performs no action whose record matters. The server records what it served only when it refused it.
